models.name: todo_app_system_settings
models.description:
Global configuration and feature flag entries for the todoApp backend.

This table stores system-wide settings such as per-user maximum todo limits, enabling or disabling optional features, and other cross-cutting configuration that is not tied to a specific user or todo item. Each row represents one named setting with a unique key, a typed raw value, and optional metadata for description and grouping.

Application logic reads these settings to control behavior at runtime, for example enforcing the maximum number of active todos per member user or enabling minimal state-based filtering. Operators can manage entries independently via dedicated administration interfaces without touching core business entities like users or todos.

Settings are soft deletable to allow safe deprecation while preserving audit history. No foreign keys are used since settings are global and not owned by any actor or business entity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description:
Primary key.

Uniquely identifies a system setting record in the todoApp backend. Generated as a UUID for global uniqueness across environments.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description:
Unique business key for the setting.

Used by application code to look up configuration values, such as "max_active_todos_per_user" or "enable_state_filtering". Must be unique across all settings.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description:
Raw value of the setting stored as a string.

Application logic interprets this value according to the associated type field. Examples include numeric limits ("10000"), boolean flags ("true"), or other scalar configuration values.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description:
Semantic type of the setting value.

Indicates how the application should interpret the `value` field, for example "int", "boolean", "string", or "double". This keeps the table normalized while allowing strongly typed handling in business logic.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of the setting.

Describes the purpose, usage, and impact of the configuration entry so operators understand how it affects todoApp behavior.

plainFields.name: group
plainFields.description:
Optional logical group or category for the setting.

Helps organize settings into domains such as "limits", "features", or "experimental" for easier management and discovery in administration tools.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description:
Flag indicating whether this setting is currently active.

When false, application logic may ignore the setting or fall back to defaults, allowing operators to disable specific configuration entries without deleting them.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the setting record was created.

Used for audit purposes and for understanding when a configuration entry was introduced to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the setting record was last updated.

Updated whenever any business field of the setting changes so operators can track recent configuration modifications.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the setting.

When set, the setting is considered logically removed from active use but remains in the database for historical reference or recovery if allowed by policy.

models.name: todo_app_guestusers
models.description:
Guest user concept representation for unauthenticated visitors.

Models the conceptual actor type "guestUser" used in authorization logic and analytics, even though guests do not authenticate or own personal data directly. This table allows the system to persist optional identifiers or metadata for guests if needed in the future, while keeping them separate from authenticated member and admin accounts.

Guest users never own todos and never have sessions; they are treated as anonymous or transient actors by the business rules.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the guest user concept record.

plainFields.name: external_ref
plainFields.description: Optional external reference or correlation identifier for this guest concept, such as an anonymous analytics or tracking ID. May be null when no persistent guest identity is needed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when this guest concept record was created. Used for basic auditing and retention decisions.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating the last time this guest concept record was updated. Allows tracking of the latest interaction time if metadata is ever extended.

models.name: todo_app_memberusers
models.description:
Authenticated member users who own personal todo items.

Represents the primary end-user actor of the todoApp service. Each member user has a unique account used for authentication and owns a private collection of todos in the business domain (referenced via {@link todo_app_todos}).

Member accounts include basic identity and authentication data (email and password hash) along with status flags and timestamps for lifecycle management such as activation and blocking.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the member user account.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Member user email address used as the primary login identifier and for communication. Must be unique across all member users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Password hash derived from the member user password using a secure one-way hashing algorithm. Plaintext passwords are never stored.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Optional human-friendly name or nickname displayed in user interfaces. May be null for minimal implementations that use only email as identifier.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Business status of the member account. Typical values include 'active', 'blocked', or 'disabled', and they govern whether todo operations are permitted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when the member user account was created. Used for auditing and ordering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating the last time account data was updated. Reflects profile or status changes.

models.name: todo_app_adminusers
models.description:
Administrative users responsible for monitoring and maintaining the todoApp service.

Represents internal operators who may access service-level information and perform exceptional maintenance or policy enforcement actions. Admin users authenticate separately from members and may have stricter credential management policies.

Admin accounts do not own member-facing todos but may read or delete them under explicit policies. This table stores admin identity and authentication information alongside lifecycle status.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the admin user account.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Admin email address used as primary login identifier for administrative access. Must be unique among admin users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Password hash for the admin account, created using a secure one-way hashing algorithm. Plaintext passwords are never stored.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable name for the admin, used in logs and dashboards for accountability and identification.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Operational status of the admin account, such as 'active', 'suspended', or 'disabled'. Controls whether the admin can sign in and perform operations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating when the admin user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating the last time administrative account information was changed.

models.name: todo_app_memberuser_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for member users of the todoApp service.

Implements the standardized per-actor session table pattern for authenticated members. Each record represents an authenticated session created when a member logs in. Sessions capture minimal connection context such as IP address and request URLs, and they track temporal validity through creation and expiration timestamps.

Sessions are subsidiary to {@link todo_app_memberusers} and are typically managed by authentication flows, not direct user CRUD. They are used for tracing actions and enforcing logout or session revocation policies.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the member user session.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_memberuser_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the owning member user account. {@link todo_app_memberusers.id}. Multiple sessions may exist for a single member.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which this session was established. Used for security analysis and anomaly detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL (href) that was requested when the session was created. Provides contextual information about the entry point.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL provided by the client when the session started. Useful for understanding navigation paths and origin.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created, indicating the start time of authenticated access.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was explicitly terminated. Null while the session remains active.

models.name: todo_app_adminuser_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for administrative users of the todoApp service.

Follows the standardized session table pattern for admin actors. Each record represents an authenticated admin session used to perform monitoring or maintenance tasks. The table captures connection context and validity periods for audit and security purposes.

Sessions are subsidiary to {@link todo_app_adminusers} and are managed by authentication components rather than regular application CRUD flows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the admin user session.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_adminuser_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the admin user who owns this session. {@link todo_app_adminusers.id}. One admin may have multiple parallel sessions.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address used when this administrative session was initiated. Supports security monitoring and incident investigation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL that was accessed at the moment the administrative session was created. Captures the entry point context.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL reported by the client when the admin session started. Helps identify navigation patterns and origins.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of session creation, indicating when admin authentication succeeded.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin session expired or was revoked. Null while the session remains active.

models.name: todo_app_todos
models.description:
Personal todo items owned by a single member user.

This table stores the minimal but complete representation of each todo in the system. Every row represents one actionable task that belongs to exactly one member user from {@link todo_app_memberusers} and is never shared between users.

Each todo contains human-readable text (title and optional description), a simple lifecycle state (such as active, completed, or deleted), and key timestamps used for ordering and enforcing business rules. Optional fields like due_date and completed_at support basic productivity workflows while maintaining a minimal schema.

Application logic uses this table for all core todo operations: creation, listing, filtering by state, viewing details, updating content, marking as completed, reopening, and deleting. Soft deletion is modeled via deleted_at so that deleted todos are excluded from normal lists but may be retained internally according to retention policies.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the todo item. Universally unique identifier for each todo row.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_memberuser_id
foreignFields.description: Owner of this todo item. References the member user who created and manages the todo. {@link todo_app_memberusers.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short human-readable title of the todo. Required, non-empty text that summarizes what needs to be done.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional longer free-text description that provides additional details about the todo. May be null or an empty string when no extra detail is provided.

plainFields.name: state
plainFields.description: Business state of the todo item. Expected values are conceptually "active" (or "pending"), "completed", or treated as deleted when deleted_at is set. Used for filtering lists and enforcing lifecycle rules.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional target date and time by which the user intends to complete the todo. When null, the todo has no explicit due date.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was first created. Set once at insertion time and used for chronological ordering and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this todo, including content edits and state changes. Used for ordering and concurrency-friendly business logic.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was last transitioned into the completed state. Null when the todo has never been completed or has been reopened without re-completion.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was logically deleted. Null while the todo is considered active or completed and visible in normal lists. Non-null values indicate soft deletion and remove the todo from user-facing queries.
